'''Exoskeleton''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in {{2|Hive}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Exoskeleton}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Skitter
|Intent = Attack1
|Effect = Deals 1 damage (×3;{{Asc2|9|×4}}).
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Mandibles
|Intent = Attack2
|Effect = Deals (8;{{Asc2|9|9}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Enrage
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Exoskeletons appear in groups of 3 or 4. Each one's opening move depends on its position in the group: 
* The first uses {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Skitter}}
* The second uses {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Mandibles}}
* The third uses {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Enrage}}
* The fourth (if present) randomly picks {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Skitter}} or {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Mandibles}}.


* After {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Skitter}}, the next move is randomly {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Skitter}} or {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Mandibles}} (cannot repeat the same move twice in a row). 
* After {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Mandibles}}, it always uses {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Enrage}}. 
* After {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Enrage}}, the next move is randomly {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Skitter}} or {{Int2|Exoskeleton|Mandibles}}.

== Useful Cards ==
* Large amounts of {{BD2|Strength}} or expensive, high-damage cards like {{C2|Bludgeon}} are less effective than usual against the '''Exoskeletons''', as each hit is capped at 9 damage no matter how much it would normally deal.
* Multihitting attacks like {{C2|Sword Boomerang}} can benefit more than other cards from '''Strength''' because each hit can individually deal up to 9 damage.
* Attacks like {{C2|Breakthrough}} or {{C2|Crush Under}} can hit all enemies at once.
* Any source of {{BD2|Doom}} can bypass the damage cap, as it simply kills enemies at end of turn rather than damaging them. The "Kill enemies" effect on {{C2|End of Days}} will similarly ignore '''Hard to Kill'''.
* {{BD2|Thorns}} from cards like {{C2|Abrasive}} will deal damage each time any of the '''Exoskeletons''' attack, and multiple times when they use '''Skitter'''.
